newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Nov U.S. car sales fall 3.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Nov U.S. car sales fall 3.5 pct.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo on Monday said car sales in the U.S. in November fell 3.5 percent to 6,511.
In the 11 month period U.S. sales were flat at 82,842, a fall of 0.3 percent compared with the same 1995 period, Volvo spokesman Ulf Thorne told Reuters.
"We hope that for the full-year 1996 we can match the 1995 and now this looks promising," Thorne said.

Sales of the 850 and the 960-series are still increasing. Sales for the Volvo 850 rose 15 percent so far this year and for the Volvo 960 they rose 28 percent. Volvo has not yet sold its 940 model in the U.S..
"We have strengthened our position in the larger car segment in the U.S.. Both the 850 and the 900 are included in this," Thorne said.
In Canada Volvo Car's sales fell sharply in November, 28.9 percent to 552 units. "But November last year was a very good month," Thorne said.
In the first 11 months of this year, Volvo sold 7,085 cars in Canada, a fall of 5.9 percent compared with the same 1995 period.
